JobsPost.title: POST /jobs
JobsPost.description: Canonical job submission. Each entry in `sources[]` is a single source file plus the ordered `steps[]` to run on it. Step types compatible with the source's auto-detected fileType are kept; incompatible steps are recorded as `skipped` in the audit log. Async (201) by default; set `sync: true` to wait up to ~27 s for completion (200) or 202 + `pending: true` on timeout. An optional `webhook` is called when the job reaches a terminal status regardless of sync mode.

sources.description: List of source files to process. Each becomes its own Task under a single Job. `steps` is required on each unless `ruleId`, `workflowId` or `previewWorkflow` decides them.

ruleId.description: Optional Rule id (rule_xxx). When present the Rule is authoritative: `sources[].steps` are discarded and the pipeline expands the Rule's matching accept entry once each file's type is known. A draft rule works too, so it can be tried on real files before it is published.

workflowId.description: Run the files through a workflow's intake (wf_xxx), as the storefront does for a product mapped to it: its intake rule replaces `ruleId` and `sources[].steps`. A draft workflow works too, so it can be tried before it is published.

previewWorkflow.description: Run the files through an unsaved workflow: the full workflow record, optionally with its rule embedded as `rule` (or `intake.rule`) instead of `intake.ruleId`. Both are kept for a day so the job can be read, then discarded. Use it to try a change to a workflow or rule before saving it. Validated against the workflow (and rule) schemas.

sync.description: When true, wait up to ~27 s for the job to reach a terminal status. Returns 200 with `{ job }` on completion or 202 with `pending: true` on timeout. Default false (async 201).

context.description: What the customer configured for this order — the finished size, how many pages, which finish. Applied to the resolved preflight profile before the file is judged, so the same Rule can serve every size of a product instead of one Rule per size. Everything the context does not mention (colour, structure, fonts, image quality) still comes from the saved profile. A check the profile has switched OFF is never switched on by supplying a value here. Omit the whole object to use the profile exactly as saved.

artworkSize.description: Finished (trim) size of the product ordered. Sets the allowed page size, and the print target that makes effective-DPI checks meaningful for raster uploads. Both dimensions are required for the page-size check to move — a width alone would widen the check to 'anything this wide', so it is ignored.

pageCount.description: How many pages this order expects. Set min === max for an exact count (e.g. a double-sided card is 2).

fileCount.description: How many separate files this order expects. Note this is NOT the order quantity — five identical banners is still one file.

bleed.description: Bleed the chosen finish requires — a hemmed banner needs far more than one trimmed to size. Moves both the bleed-box requirement and the matching content-coverage allowance together.

safety.description: Safe margin the chosen finish requires (eyelets and pole pockets eat into it). Unlike the others this threshold reaches the analyzer, so changing it on an existing job forces a full re-check rather than a re-read of the stored report.

params.description: Step-type-specific parameters. Validated by the action Lambda; unknown keys are ignored.

label.description: Optional human-friendly label echoed in the audit log.

onError.description: Failure policy for this step. `halt` (default) fails the whole job if the step errors. `continue` tolerates the failure: the job still completes, its outcome becomes `warn`, and the step's error is attached as a finding — use for best-effort steps (e.g. a colour conversion the engine may refuse) where the customer should still receive their file.

url.description: Public or authenticated URL of the file.

source.description: URL or base64 file contents (alias for url|file).

file.description: Inline base64-encoded file contents. String length must be ≤ 9.3 MB. Prefer `url` or `fileRef` for large files.

fileRef.description: Reference id returned by POST /uploads. Use for large files to avoid body-size limits.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers sent when fetching the URL (e.g. Authorization).

params.description: Free-form per-source extras carried through to the audit log.

steps.description: Ordered list of steps to run on this source. Steps execute sequentially; the runner threads a `currentArtifact` reference between steps.

name.description: Original filename hint (used when `file` is provided).

webhook.description: Endpoint called when the job reaches a terminal status (done | skipped | error). Inspect the separate `outcome` field for the verdict.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint to POST the job result to.

headers.description: Optional headers sent with the webhook callback (e.g. Authorization).

metaData.description: Free-form caller context echoed back on the response and on webhook callbacks. JSON-serialized payload must be ≤ 4 KB.

JobsPreflightPost.title: POST /jobs/preflight
JobsPreflightPost.description: Submit one or more files for preflight. By default the response is 201 Accepted and the job runs asynchronously. Set `sync: true` to wait up to ~27 s for the result (200 on completion, 202 + `pending: true` on timeout). An optional `webhook` is called when the job reaches a terminal status regardless of sync mode.

sources.description: List of files to preflight. Each becomes its own Task under a single Job. Even a single file must be wrapped in an array.

sync.description: When true, the request waits for the job to complete (up to ~27 s). Returns 200 with `{ job }` on success, or 202 with `pending: true` on timeout. The default is false (async 201).

context.description: What the customer configured for this order — the finished size, how many pages, which finish. Applied to each source's `profileId` before the file is judged, so one profile can serve every size of a product instead of one profile per size. Everything the context does not mention (colour, structure, fonts, image quality) still comes from the saved profile, and a check the profile has switched OFF is never switched on by supplying a value here. Has no effect on sources with no `profileId` — those already run every check. Omit to use the profile exactly as saved.

artworkSize.description: Finished (trim) size of the product ordered. Sets the allowed page size, and the print target that makes effective-DPI checks meaningful for raster uploads. Both dimensions are required for the page-size check to move — a width alone would widen the check to 'anything this wide', so it is ignored.

pageCount.description: How many pages this order expects. Set min === max for an exact count (e.g. a double-sided card is 2).

fileCount.description: How many separate files this order expects. Note this is NOT the order quantity — five identical banners is still one file.

bleed.description: Bleed the chosen finish requires — a hemmed banner needs far more than one trimmed to size. Moves both the bleed-box requirement and the matching content-coverage allowance together.

safety.description: Safe margin the chosen finish requires (eyelets and pole pockets eat into it). Unlike the others this threshold reaches the analyzer, so changing it on an existing job forces a full re-check rather than a re-read of the stored report.

url.description: Public or authenticated URL of the file.

file.description: Inline base64-encoded file contents. String length must be ≤ 9.3 MB (the ~7 MB decoded equivalent). Prefer `url` or `fileRef` for large files.

fileRef.description: Reference id returned by POST /uploads. Use for large files to avoid body-size limits.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers sent when fetching the URL (e.g. Authorization).

profileId.description: Optional preflight profile id for a specific preflight profile (yours, or a published `preflight_standard_*`). Omit to run every check we cover for the file's kind.

name.description: Original filename hint (used when `file` is provided).

webhook.description: Endpoint called when the job reaches a terminal status (done | skipped | error). Inspect the separate `outcome` field for the verdict.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint to POST the job result to.

headers.description: Optional headers sent with the webhook callback (e.g. Authorization).

metaData.description: Free-form caller context echoed back on the response and on webhook callbacks. JSON-serialized payload must be ≤ 4 KB.

JobsOptimizePost.title: POST /jobs/optimize
JobsOptimizePost.description: Optimize one or more files. Each source carries its own `params`, namespaced by file type: `params.pdf` for PDFs (DynaPDF pipeline) and `params.raster` for bitmaps (Sharp + fal.ai pipeline). Exactly one namespace per source is consumed — the server picks based on the detected file type. Mixed batches (PDF + raster in the same request) are supported. The request is synchronous by default — the response is 200 with `{ job }` on completion, or 202 with `pending: true` if the job does not finish within ~27 s. An optional `webhook` is called when the job reaches a terminal status.

sources.description: List of files to optimize. Each item may include a `params` object describing which optimizations to apply. Even a single file must be wrapped in an array.

async.description: When true, return 201 immediately with `{ job, pending: true }` and let the webhook (if any) deliver the terminal result. When false (default), the request is synchronous — 200 on completion, or 202 with `pending: true` if the job does not finish within ~27 s.

oneOf.description: Public or authenticated URL of the file.

url.description: Public or authenticated URL of the file.

file.description: Inline base64-encoded file contents. String length must be ≤ 9.3 MB (the ~7 MB decoded equivalent). Prefer `url` or `fileRef` for large files.

fileRef.description: Reference id returned by POST /uploads. Use for large files to avoid body-size limits.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers sent when fetching the URL (e.g. Authorization).

name.description: Original filename hint (used when `file` is provided).

optimizeParams.description: Per-source optimization options, namespaced by file type. Exactly one of `pdf` / `raster` is consumed per source — the server selects the namespace matching the detected file type. Future file types (e.g. `vector`) will slot in alongside. An empty object is invalid; omit `params` entirely if no options are needed.

pdfOptimizeParams.description: PDF optimization options applied via DynaPDF. All fields are optional; an empty object performs a stream-rebuild only (still typically reduces size). Options may interact: see the `dependsOn` notes per field.

flattenLayers.description: Flatten optional content groups (layers) into a single visible layer.

rasterOptimizeParams.description: Raster optimization options application. Pipeline order is fixed: removeBg → upscale → crop → grayscale → colorspace → flatten → resize → embedIcc → convert. All fields are optional; an empty object is a no-op transcode of the source format.

rasterRemoveBg.description: AI background removal. Produces an RGBA result with the background pixels turned transparent. Combine with `flatten` to composite onto a solid color, or with `convert: { format:'png' }` to preserve transparency.

enabled.description: Set true to run the BiRefNet model.

rasterUpscale.description: AI upscale. The scale factor is derived in this order: (a) explicit `scale`; (b) `target_width_px` and/or `target_height_px` → scale per axis = `target_px / source_px` (no `minDpi` required); (c) `minDpi` + `target_width_mm` and/or `target_height_mm` → required pixels per axis = `minDpi * mm / 25.4`; final scale = max of per-axis required scales so both dimensions meet the floor; (d) `minDpi` alone + the image's embedded DPI tag → `minDpi / density`. If none of these apply the op is skipped (`reason: 'no_dpi_basis'`). If the computed scale is ≤ 1 the image already meets the floor and the op is skipped (`reason: 'already_at_dpi'`). Capped at 4× to bound cost and latency. When `minDpi` is supplied the encoded output is tagged with that density via Sharp `withMetadata`, regardless of whether the upscale itself ran.

minDpi.description: Minimum effective DPI the upscaled image must hit. Primary driver — most callers should set this and let the runtime work out the scale from `target_width_mm` or the source's tagged DPI. Also written to the output's density metadata.

target_width_mm.description: Target horizontal print size in millimetres. Combined with `minDpi` to compute the required pixel width: `ceil(minDpi * target_width_mm / 25.4)`.

target_height_mm.description: Target vertical print size in millimetres. Combined with `minDpi` to compute the required pixel height: `ceil(minDpi * target_height_mm / 25.4)`. May be supplied alongside `target_width_mm`; the larger required scale wins.

target_width_px.description: Target horizontal pixel count. Direct pixel target — does not require `minDpi`. May be combined with `target_height_px`; the larger required scale wins. Takes precedence over the mm-based path.

target_height_px.description: Target vertical pixel count. Direct pixel target — does not require `minDpi`. May be combined with `target_width_px`; the larger required scale wins. Takes precedence over the mm-based path.

scale.description: Explicit scale factor. Only useful when the caller knows the source pixel dimensions — most printers should rely on `minDpi` instead.

rasterCrop.description: Centered crop to one of a set of allowed aspect ratios. The runtime picks the allowed ratio (or its inverse, for portrait/landscape match) closest to the source's current ratio. No-op when the source already matches within `tolerance`.

ratios.description: Allowed aspect ratios. Strings may use `:`, `/` or `x` (e.g. `"4:3"`, `"16/9"`); numbers are treated as width÷height.

tolerance.description: Allowed deviation between source ratio and target before cropping.

rasterGrayscale.description: Convert to grayscale. Independent of `colorspace`: use this for the simple 'desaturate' case; use `colorspace: { target:'grayscale' }` when you also need ICC handling.

rasterColorspace.description: Convert the working colorspace. When `iccAlias` is supplied the destination ICC is also embedded in the output (otherwise Sharp's untagged colour transform is used).

target.description: Destination colorspace.

iccAlias.description: Bundled ICC alias (e.g. `fogra39`, `swop`, `apple-rgb`) or a .icc filename present in the raster Lambda's profiles directory.

rasterFlatten.description: Composite a transparent image onto a solid colour, dropping the alpha channel.

rasterResize.description: Pixel-dimension resize. The runtime applies the constraint that bounds the image — `maxWidth`/`maxHeight` shrink oversized images, `minWidth`/`minHeight` enlarge undersized ones. Aspect ratio is preserved by default (`fit: 'inside'`).

rasterEmbedIcc.description: Embed an ICC profile in the output without changing pixel values. Use `colorspace.iccAlias` if you also need the conversion.

rasterConvert.description: Re-encode to a different format. Output mime type and extension are inferred from the target format.

rasterBitDepth.description: Requested minimum bits-per-channel. Informational at the pipeline layer — actual depth is determined by the chosen encoder/colourspace.

snapRichBlack.description: Rewrite every DeviceCMYK fill or stroke whose C, M and Y channels all reach `threshold` to pure K (0, 0, 0, 1). Runs in a separate pikepdf pre-optimize pass before the DynaPDF pipeline so other colors (brand spots, photos, ICC-tagged values, Separation / DeviceN) pass through untouched. Only the `k` / `K` shortcut ops and `scn` / `SCN` under an explicit `cs` / `CS DeviceCMYK` are rewritten.

enabled.description: Set true to run the rich-black snap pre-optimize pass.

threshold.description: Minimum component value (0–1) on C, M AND Y for a CMYK color to be classified as rich black. Default 0.85 matches the preflight detector.

upscaleImages.description: AI-upscale placed images whose effective resolution falls below `targetDpi`. Runs in a separate pikepdf pre-pass before the DynaPDF pipeline: each low-DPI image is extracted, upscaled via fal.ai recraft crisp, and re-embedded (soft masks are resized locally to match). RGB, gray and indexed images only; CMYK/JPX sources are left untouched and reported. Images needing more than `maxScale` are upscaled to the cap and reported as below target.

enabled.description: Set true to run the upscale-images pre-pass.

targetDpi.description: Effective-DPI floor each placed image should reach.

maxImages.description: Maximum images upscaled per document, worst DPI first; the rest are reported as skipped.

bleed.description: Add bleed to the page. The finished page — or the source MediaBox when no usable TrimBox is present — is treated as the trim; `required_mm` of bleed is added beyond it on the selected edges and the media/bleed/trim boxes are set accordingly. `fill` controls how the new bleed strip is populated. mirror/scale run in a separate fc-repairs-bleed-fill pass (which also flattens viewer-visible annotations into the artwork) before the DynaPDF optimize pass; fill:'none' is resolved inline.

required_mm.description: Bleed margin in millimetres added beyond the trim on each selected edge (e.g. 3).

fill.description: How to populate the new bleed strip. 'none' = stamp boxes only (artwork must already reach the sheet edge); 'mirror' = reflect edge artwork outward across the trim; 'scale' = enlarge page content so it overflows the trim.

sides.description: Which edges to apply bleed to. Default ['all']. Ignored for fill:'scale' (centric scale always affects all edges).

outputIntent.description: Embed an ICC profile as the document's output intent. Used by prepress workflows to declare the intended printing condition. The profile is referenced either by alias (mapped to a bundled ICC in the repairs Lambda — e.g. 'fogra39', 'swop', 'pso-coated') or by absolute path to a .icc file. Applied at the end of optimize, immediately before save.

profile.description: ICC profile alias or absolute path to a .icc file.

registry.description: Registry URL for the output condition. Informational.

boundingBoxes.description: Set the trim and/or crop box as per-side margins (insets) from the page's media box, before optimization. At most one entry per box (trim, crop) — hence max 2. Each box is resolved per page against the source PDF, so one set of margins works on any page size. Margins are in points (1 pt = 1/72 inch), measured inward from the media edge. If a box ends up under 1 unit wide Filecheck deletes it from the page. To add or expand bleed (which also sets the trim for you), use `bleed` instead.

boundingBoxSourceRelative.description: Set the trim or crop box as per-side margins (insets) from the media box, resolved per page against the source PDF before import — so one set of margins works on any page size. Margins are in points (1 pt = 1/72 inch); positive = inward, negative = outward, 0 = flush with the media edge. Omitted sides default to 0. `expand` is a uniform shorthand (note: positive `expand` grows OUTWARD — opposite sign to the per-side fields) used internally by the trim autofix. When pageResize is also active the source rect is translated by the source media origin and multiplied by the resize scale before the margins are applied.

box.description: Which page boundary to set. (media is implicit and required by PDF; bleed is handled by the `bleed` option.)

source.description: Reference box the margins are measured from. Always the media box — the only box guaranteed to exist on every page.

expand.description: Uniform grow (positive) / shrink (negative) on all four sides, in points. (1 pt = 1/72 inch)

top.description: Per-side inset in points for the TOP edge: positive moves it inward, negative outward, from the resolved source rect. Combines additively with `expand`. (1 pt = 1/72 inch)

bottom.description: Per-side inset in points for the BOTTOM edge (positive = inward). Combines with `expand`.

left.description: Per-side inset in points for the LEFT edge (positive = inward). Combines with `expand`.

right.description: Per-side inset in points for the RIGHT edge (positive = inward). Combines with `expand`.

page.description: 1-based source page. Omit to apply to every page.

pageResize.description: Resize all pages during import. Supply EITHER explicit `scaleX`/`scaleY` factors, OR a target `width`+`height` in PDF user units (pt), OR a named `format`. A single uniform scale is computed from page 1 of the source and applied document-wide (Filecheck's import-time scaling is whole-document); each output page's media box is then independently set to its own (sourceDims x scale) when only direct factors are given, or to the exact target rectangle when a size-based target is used.

mode.description: How to fit content to a size target. `scale` (default) applies the same factor to both axes so the source fits inside the target without distortion (may leave blank margins). `stretch` uses independent X/Y factors to exactly hit the target (may distort). Ignored when only `scaleX`/`scaleY` are supplied.

scaleX.description: Horizontal scale factor (1.0 = no change). Used only when no size target (`width`/`height`/`format`) is supplied.

scaleY.description: Vertical scale factor (defaults to `scaleX` if omitted). Used only when no size target is supplied.

width.description: Target page width in PDF user units (1 pt = 1/72 inch). Requires `height` as well.

height.description: Target page height in PDF user units. Requires `width` as well.

format.description: Named paper format. Resolved against `orientation`. Mutually exclusive with `width`/`height`.

hairlines.description: Increase the width of thin lines that would otherwise drop out or render inconsistently on press. Critical for offset / flexo / large-format output where 0-width or sub-pixel strokes are unsafe.

minWidth.description: Minimum stroke width in points (1 pt = 1/72 inch). Lines thinner than this are widened to this value. Common values: 0.25 (~0.09 mm) for sheetfed offset, 0.5 (~0.18 mm) for flexo, 0.75-1.0 for large-format / screen printing.

ignoreZeroWidth.description: Leave PDF zero-width strokes (`0 w`, render as one device pixel) unchanged. Off by default — zero-width strokes are the most common hairline-rendering hazard.

zeroWidthOnly.description: Only widen real zero-width strokes (`0 w`); leave all other thin-but-nonzero strokes alone. Use when designers intentionally specified narrow strokes you don't want altered.

scaleImages.description: Downsample raster images that exceed the target resolution. Activated when `targetRes` is present — no `enabled` flag needed.

skipMasked.description: Skip images that have a color mask.

skipSizeCheck.description: Always write the downsampled image even if the result would be larger than the original.

minRes.description: Resolution threshold (DPI). Images at or below this resolution are not scaled. Optional — if omitted per channel, defaults to targetRes + 1 (i.e. only images strictly above the target are touched).

bw.description: Target DPI for 1-bit black & white images.

compression.description: Image compression filters and quality. Filter codes: `flate` (lossless, default for line art), `jpeg` (lossy, photos), `jpeg2000` (lossy, slow), `ccitt4` (lossless, 1-bit fax), `jbig2` (lossless/lossy, 1-bit, best for scanned text).

bwFilter.description: Compression filter for 1-bit black & white images.

use1BitJBIG2.description: Recompress 1-bit images with JBIG2 (very strong for scanned text). Skips images already JBIG2-encoded.

recompressJBIG2.description: Force re-encode of 1-bit images even if already JBIG2-encoded. Only meaningful if `use1BitJBIG2` is true.

colorConversion.description: Convert images, text and vector graphics to a single device color space. To convert images as well, the `ConvertAllColors` flag is required (set via `convertSpecialSpaces`) — otherwise only text and vectors are converted. Critical for print workflows that require a specific output color space (e.g. CMYK or grayscale) and for RGB files that contain a mix of embedded-color and device-color content (e.g. RGB images but CMYK vectors).

target.description: Target device color space.

convertSpecialSpaces.description: Also convert Separation, DeviceN and NChannel color spaces. Enabling this will force image conversions for images that do have special color spaces.

preserve.description: Color-space families to leave unchanged when converting. Critical for prepress: `separation` keeps spot inks (Pantone, varnish, white, metallics), `deviceN` / `nchannel` keep multi-ink builds, `icc` keeps calibrated profiles untouched, `separationAll` keeps the special `All` separation (used for registration / die marks).

excludeColorSpaces.description: Named color spaces (typically spot ink names like `PANTONE 185 C`, `Cutter`, `White`, `Varnish`) to exclude from conversion. Match is case-insensitive against the color-space name as declared in the PDF.

excludeMode.description: Interpretation of `excludeColorSpaces`: `exclude` (default) skips the listed spaces and converts everything else; `only` does the inverse — converts only the listed spaces and leaves all others alone. Useful for one-off normalizations (e.g. convert a single rogue RGB spot back to CMYK).

replaceJpeg2000WithJpeg.description: Recompress converted JPEG 2000 images with JPEG (~10× faster, near-identical quality).

onOverprint.description: Behavior when a page contains overprinted objects: `fail` aborts the job (safest for print-critical files — color appearance can change unpredictably), `skip` leaves overprinted objects in their original space, `convert` converts everything anyway (may shift colors on press).

grayTo1Bit.description: Convert grayscale images to 1-bit black & white. Useful for scanned faxes that came in as gray.

useOtsuFilter.description: Use the Otsu threshold algorithm (better for scanned content). Only meaningful if `enabled` is true.

textToOutlines.description: Convert text into vector outlines. The result has no extractable/searchable text.

nonEmbeddedOnly.description: Outline only text in non-embedded fonts (preserves searchability where the font is embedded). Only meaningful if `enabled` is true.

strip.description: Remove non-essential objects to reduce file size.

thumbnails.description: Remove embedded page thumbnails (viewers regenerate on demand).

privateData.description: Remove application-private data from pages, templates and images.

invisiblePaths.description: Remove vector paths that produce no visible output (`n` operator).

batesNumbers.description: Remove Bates numbering and any associated headers/footers.

headerFooter.description: Remove headers and footers that were not added as Bates numbers.

annotations.description: Skip all annotations at import (text notes, sticky notes, links, stamps, etc.). Signature widgets live under `formFields`; remove those via the dedicated decrypt pass.

formFields.description: Skip the interactive form (AcroForm + XFA) at import. Covers form fields, NeedAppearances, and any embedded XFA payload.

attachments.description: Skip file attachments / embedded files at import.

javascript.description: Skip document-level JavaScript and JavaScript actions at import.

bookmarks.description: Skip the document outline (bookmarks) at import.

webhook.description: Endpoint called when the job reaches a terminal status (done | skipped | error). Inspect the separate `outcome` field for the verdict.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint to POST the job result to.

headers.description: Optional headers sent with the webhook callback (e.g. Authorization).

metaData.description: Free-form caller context echoed back on the response and on webhook callbacks. JSON-serialized payload must be ≤ 4 KB.

JobsValidatePost.title: POST /jobs/validate
JobsValidatePost.description: Validate one or more files against PDF/A or PDF/UA conformance levels. Each source carries its own `profile` (one or more codes). The request is synchronous by default — the response is 200 with `{ job }` on completion, or 202 with `pending: true` if the job does not finish within ~27 s. An optional `webhook` is called when the job reaches a terminal status.

sources.description: List of files to validate. Each item must include a `profile` field. Even a single file must be wrapped in an array.

async.description: When true, return 201 immediately with `{ job, pending: true }` and let the webhook (if any) deliver the terminal result. When false (default), the request is synchronous — 200 on completion, or 202 with `pending: true` if the job does not finish within ~27 s.

profileCode.description: PDF/A or PDF/UA conformance level code, or 'auto' to let the validator infer the closest matching profile from the file itself. PDF/A: 1a 1b 2a 2b 2u 3a 3b 3u 4 4e 4f. PDF/UA: ua1 ua2.

oneOf.description: Public or authenticated URL of the file.

url.description: Public or authenticated URL of the file.

file.description: Inline base64-encoded file contents. String length must be ≤ 9.3 MB (the ~7 MB decoded equivalent). Prefer `url` or `fileRef` for large files.

fileRef.description: Reference id returned by POST /uploads. Use for large files to avoid body-size limits.

profile.description: One or more conformance level codes to validate this file against. Optional — when omitted, defaults to 'auto' which infers the closest matching profile from the file itself.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers sent when fetching the URL (e.g. Authorization).

name.description: Original filename hint (used when `file` is provided).

webhook.description: Endpoint called when the job reaches a terminal status (done | skipped | error). Inspect the separate `outcome` field for the verdict.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint to POST the job result to.

headers.description: Optional headers sent with the webhook callback (e.g. Authorization).

metaData.description: Free-form caller context echoed back on the response and on webhook callbacks. JSON-serialized payload must be ≤ 4 KB.

items.description: Specific autofix items to apply; omit to let Filecheck choose defaults.

repreflight.description: Re-run preflight after autofix to confirm the result.

mimeType.description: Content type of the file you intend to upload.

sizeBytes.description: Expected size in bytes. Capped at 500 MB.

fileRef.description: Pass this as a job source.

type.description: preflight, repreflight, autofix, optimize, validate, previews, proof

status.description: idle, incomplete, uploading, processing, ready, partial, rejected

results.description: Aggregated validate / preflight / optimize results on non-lean responses.

Run.description: A flattened per-file view returned by ?expand=runs.

Connector.title: Connector
Connector.description: Wires a store's own product page to the FileCheck upload element (the Element embedded on WooCommerce, Shopify, PrestaShop, OpenCart or custom product pages), in both directions, with no custom code. Read entries take what the shopper chose on the page (banner width and height, a size dropdown, number of pages, single or double sided, finishing such as hem and eyelets) and use it to override the size-dependent checks of the product's rule and preflight profile for that upload: required artwork size, page count, file count, bleed and safe margin. Write entries push what FileCheck measured in the upload (page count, page width, height or area, color or mono page counts) or the rule's default size into the page's own inputs (quantity, width, height, area), so the store recalculates the price from the actual file. A connector never accepts, rejects or prices anything itself; the rule decides acceptance and the store stays in charge of price. It runs in the shopper's browser: the Element applies a connector passed to it as its `connector` option (this record's JSON, as returned by GET /connectors/{id}); handing the Element only a connectorId is reserved and not resolved yet. No other FileCheck record points at a connector; the cart plugins store the chosen connector id per product.

title.description: Name shown in the dashboard and in the cart plugins' per-product connector picker, e.g. "Banner size sync". The dashboard will not save a connector without one.

description.description: A note for the print shop: which products and which theme this connector was built for.

entries.description: The connector's rules, both directions in one list, told apart by `type`: "read" (product page to FileCheck) or "write" (FileCheck to product page; an entry without `type` is a write entry). Entries run in order; when several read entries set the same value, the later one wins.

bindings.description: Legacy copy of the write entries, kept for Element versions released before `entries` existed; readers use it only when `entries` is empty. Omit it in new connectors, or keep it identical to the write entries in `entries` (the dashboard writes it that way on every save).

schemaVersion.description: Record format version written by the dashboard editor (currently 1). Omit it.

tags.description: Free-form labels for organising the Library. Not used at runtime.

entry.description: One read or write rule. `type: "read"` selects the read shape; anything else (including no `type`) is a write entry.

entryId.description: Stable id for this entry, unique within the connector; it shows up in the Element's debug report (?fcdebug=1). Optional: one is generated when the dashboard opens the connector.

entryEnabled.description: Set false to keep the entry but skip it at runtime.

customSelector.description: CSS selector for the control on the product page, tried before the built-in selectors, e.g. #banner-width or select[name="attribute_pa_size"]. Leave empty to rely on the built-in selectors alone. Only used with querySelector, so the first matching element wins; an invalid selector is skipped.

rounding.description: How the converted value is rounded to `decimals`: round to nearest, floor (down) or ceil (up). With decimals null, floor and ceil round to whole numbers and round leaves the value as is.

decimals.description: Decimal places to round the converted value to (0 to 6). null means no rounding. Counts are always whole numbers.

unitName.description: Named unit: mm (millimetres), cm, m (metres), in (inches), ft (feet), pt (points, 1/72 inch).

unit.description: A unit: one of the names mm, cm, m, in, ft, pt, or a positive number giving millimetres per one unit of the page's value (25.4 for inches, 100 for decimetres).

pickedUnit.description: Read the unit from a second control on the page, for pages that pair a size box with a unit dropdown.

fromSelector.description: CSS selector of the unit control, e.g. select[name="unit"].

map.description: The unit control's option values mapped to units, e.g. { "CM": "cm", "feet": "ft", "mm": "mm" }. Matched as-is, then lower- and upper-cased. Without a map the control's value itself must be a unit name. An unrecognised value falls back to millimetres.

max.description: Highest accepted count. Use min = max for an exact count.

contextFragment.description: What one choice means for the check, in millimetres and plain counts. Each key overrides one part of the product's rule or profile for this upload (and only parts that are switched on there).

artworkSize.description: Required finished (trim) size; replaces the profile's allowed page sizes and the raster print size used for effective DPI.

pageCount.description: Required number of pages, e.g. { "min": 2, "max": 2 } for double sided; replaces the profile's page-count check.

fileCount.description: How many files the shopper must upload; replaces the rule's file cardinality.

bleed.description: Required bleed; replaces the profile's bleed and bleed-coverage checks.

required_mm.description: Bleed in mm on each edge, e.g. 25 for a hemmed banner.

safety.description: Safe margin that text must stay inside; replaces the profile's safety-margin check (the file is analyzed again when this changes).

min_mm.description: Margin in mm from the trim edge, e.g. 20 for eyelets.

readEntry.description: Product page to FileCheck: read one control the shopper sets and turn it into a requirement for the upload check. The value is re-read whenever the shopper changes the control.

field.description: What the control means. width / height: one measurement, converted to mm (drives artworkSize by default). size: one control holding both, e.g. "3000 x 1000 mm"; needs `pattern` with width and height groups (drives artworkSize). pages: number of pages (drives pageCount). files: number of separate files (drives fileCount). sides and finishing: a choice looked up in `map` (sides typically sets pageCount, finishing sets bleed and safety). Built-in selectors tried after customSelector: width: input[name="width"], #width, input[data-dimension="width"], input[name="dimension_width"], input[name="banner_width"], .product-width input (height likewise); size: select[name="size"], #size, input[name="size"], [data-option="size"]; pages: input[name="pages"], #pages, select[name="pages"], [data-option="pages"]; sides: select[name="sides"], input[name="sides"]:checked, #sides, [data-option="sides"]; files: input[name="files"], select[name="files"], [data-option="files"]; finishing: select[name="finishing"], input[name="finishing"]:checked, #finishing, [data-option="finishing"].

read.description: How to get the raw string from the control: value (the input's or select's value, falling back to its text), text (the element's text content) or attr (the attribute named in `attr`).

attr.description: Attribute to read when read is attr, e.g. data-value.

pattern.description: Optional JavaScript regular expression run on the raw string (first 512 characters). Named groups pick the numbers: width and height for a size field, e.g. (?<width>[\d.]+)\s*[x×]\s*(?<height>[\d.]+); value for counts and choices. Without named groups the first two groups are taken as width and height. When a pattern is set and does not match, the entry yields nothing (the product's own settings apply) rather than guessing.

patternFlags.description: Flags for `pattern`, e.g. i for case-insensitive.

convertFrom.description: Unit of the measurement on the page, converted to mm (width, height and size fields only; ignored for counts and choices). A unit name (mm, cm, m, in, ft, pt), a number of millimetres per page unit (e.g. 25.4), or { fromSelector, map } to read the unit from another control. Default mm.

target.description: What the value drives. Default (null) follows the field: width, height and size drive artworkSize; pages drives pageCount; files drives fileCount. A width or height entry can instead drive bleed or safety (the measurement becomes the bleed or safe margin in mm); a pages or files entry can drive pageCount or fileCount. Choice fields ignore this and use `map`.

map.description: For sides and finishing: each option value on the page (as read, also tried lower-cased) mapped to what it requires, e.g. { "single": { "pageCount": { "min": 1, "max": 1 } }, "double": { "pageCount": { "min": 2, "max": 2 } } } or { "hem_eyelets": { "bleed": { "required_mm": 25 }, "safety": { "min_mm": 20 } } }. An option missing from the map yields nothing. Ignored for other fields.

watch.description: DOM events on the control that mean the shopper changed it. Default ["input", "change"].

writeEntry.description: FileCheck to product page: write one measured fact (or the rule's default) into a control on the page. Runs after every upload status change.

type.description: Marks a write entry. Optional: entries without a type are write entries.

source.description: The value to write. pageCount: total pages across the upload. fileCount: number of accepted files. colorPageCount / monoPageCount: pages with any color or spot ink / black-only pages (nothing is written when ink was not measured). width / height: the first file's page width / height in mm. area: the first file's page area in mm². ruleWidth / ruleHeight / rulePages: the product rule's default artwork width, height (mm) and page count, written before anything is uploaded, to seed the page with the product's default size.

control.description: Which kind of control to write into; picks built-in selectors tried after customSelector. quantity: input[name="quantity"], input.quantity, #quantity, #qty, .qty, input[name="qty"], input[data-quantity], .quantity input[type="number"]. width: input[name="width"], #width, .product-width, input[data-dimension="width"], input[name="dimension_width"] (height likewise). area: input[name="area"], #area, .product-area, select[name="area"], input[data-dimension="area"]. null: use customSelector only. Either control or customSelector is required.

set.description: How to write: value (sets the input's or select's value), text (replaces the element's text) or attr (sets the attribute named in `attr`).

attr.description: Attribute to set when set is attr, e.g. data-qty.

emit.description: DOM events fired on the control after writing, so the store's own scripts (price calculators, variant pickers) notice the change. Default ["input", "change"].

convertFrom.description: Unit of the source value. Measured facts are always millimetres, so leave this at mm (the default). Ignored for counts.

convertTo.description: Unit the page's control expects for width, height and area: a unit name (mm, cm, m, in, ft, pt) or millimetres per page unit. Area is converted with the square of the factor. Ignored for counts.

Destination.title: Destination
Destination.description: Where a job's finished, print-ready files go once the job completes successfully. A destination is a reusable Library record: a workflow lists the destinations it delivers to in workflow.delivery.destinationIds (and only delivers while workflow.delivery.enabled is not false), and one destination can serve any number of workflows. `kind` picks the transport and `params` holds that transport's settings: email (download links mailed out), webhook (a JSON POST with download links, e.g. into Zapier), or one of the hotfolder kinds s3, sftp and ftp, which copy the files themselves into a folder the print shop's prepress or MIS system watches. Delivery runs once per job, after the job reaches done (never for previews or failed jobs); each destination is tried once and a failure on one does not stop the others. Files are named after the product (e.g. Business_Cards.pdf, or Business_Cards-1.pdf, Business_Cards-2.pdf when a job has several). Secret params (sftp/ftp password, sftp privateKey and passphrase, webhook headerValue) are write-only: send them as plain strings and they are encrypted on save; they read back masked as ********, and sending ******** back unchanged keeps the stored value. Use the destination test action to send a sample delivery (a one-page Sample_Product.pdf for order TEST-1001) through the real transport before pointing a workflow at it. Changing `kind` on an existing destination: also null out the old kind's params (JSON Merge Patch keeps keys you don't send).

kind.description: The transport. email: mails download links (no files attached) to an address, by default the shopper who placed the order. webhook: POSTs a JSON envelope with download links to a URL. s3: writes the files into an Amazon S3 bucket. sftp: uploads over SSH (SFTP). ftp: uploads over FTP or FTPS. s3, sftp and ftp are hotfolder kinds: they accept path tokens and metadata sidecars.

title.description: Display name in the dashboard and in delivery logs, e.g. "Prepress hotfolder (SFTP)". Optional; the dashboard falls back to the kind plus host, bucket or address.

description.description: A note for the print shop: what this destination feeds and who owns the receiving end.

params.description: The settings for `kind`; each kind accepts only its own keys. email: to, cc, bcc, replyTo, subject, attachMetadata, includeMetadata, templateId, linkExpiryHours. webhook: url (required), headerName, headerValue (secret), includeLinks, linkExpiryHours, meta. s3: bucket (required), region, access, roleArn, externalId, acl, prefix, plus the sidecar fields. sftp: host and username (required), port, password and/or privateKey (secrets, one required), passphrase (secret), path, plus the sidecar fields. ftp: host (required), port, username, password (secret), secure, path, plus the sidecar fields. Sidecar fields (s3/sftp/ftp): sidecar, sidecarFormat, sidecarTemplate, sidecarExt, includeFullReport.

secretsSet.description: Dashboard display flags saying which secret params hold a value (so the editor can show "set" without the secret). Not used for delivery and not authoritative; omit it, the dashboard derives it.

schemaVersion.description: Record format version written by the dashboard editor (currently 1). Omit it.

tags.description: Free-form labels for organising the Library. Not used for delivery.

secret.description: A write-only credential. Send the plaintext as a string; it is encrypted on save and reads back as ********. The stored, encrypted form is an object { "enc": "..." }; it only appears when a record is re-validated with the secret left untouched, so never construct one yourself. To remove a secret, send null.

sealedSecret.description: A secret as stored: encrypted by FileCheck on save. Kept unchanged when a write leaves the secret alone; never construct one yourself.

linkExpiryHours.description: How long the download links stay valid, in hours (1 to 168, i.e. at most 7 days). Not editable in the dashboard; a later save of this destination from the dashboard editor drops it back to the 24-hour default.

remotePath.description: Folder layout on the receiving end, as a static folder or a template with {tokens}. Without tokens it is a root folder and files land in <path>/orders/<orderId>/<file> (or <path>/jobs/<jobId>/<file> when the job has no order). With any {token} the template IS the whole layout and the orders/ folder is not added. Tokens ({name} or {{name}}): {orderId}, {jobId}, {jobName}, {sku}, {productId}, {product} (product name), {itemId} (order line item), {quantity}, {fileId} (alias {taskId}), {customer} (customer email), {filename} (e.g. Business_Cards.pdf), {basename} (filename without extension), {ext}, {n} (file number 1, 2, ...), {date} (YYYYMMDD, UTC), {yyyy}, {mm}, {dd}, {rand} (8 random hex chars). Values are made path-safe (characters other than letters, digits, _ . - and spaces are dropped, spaces become _, max 80 characters), and an empty or unknown token drops its folder level. If the template has neither {filename} nor {basename}, the filename is appended, so "/hotfolder/{orderId}/{sku}" writes hotfolder/ORD-1001/SKU-42/Business_Cards.pdf and "/in/{orderId}_{basename}.{ext}" names the file itself (in/ORD-1001_Business_Cards.pdf).

sidecar.description: Also deliver a metadata file next to each print file, uploaded after it so a hotfolder watching for the sidecar always finds a complete print file. Named like the print file with the sidecar extension (Business_Cards.pdf gets Business_Cards.json). Off when omitted; the dashboard turns it on for new hotfolder destinations.

sidecarFormat.description: json: FileCheck's JSON envelope (generated time, job, order with customer and shipping address, product with sku and quantity, file, and the preflight summary, evaluation and findings). custom: the text of sidecarTemplate with tokens filled in, for an MIS that expects its own XML, CSV or ticket format. Only used when sidecar is true.

sidecarTemplate.description: Body of a custom sidecar (sidecarFormat custom), e.g. <order id="{orderId}"><sku>{sku}</sku><qty>{quantity}</qty></order>. Takes every path token plus {customerName}, {orderStatus}, {currency}, {total}, {pages} (page count), {minDpi} (lowest effective image DPI), {maxTac} (max ink coverage %), {spotColors}, {verdict} (pass, warn or fail), {passCount}, {warnCount}, {failCount}. Values are inserted raw (spaces kept), and XML-escaped when sidecarExt is xml or the template starts with <. Unknown tokens become empty.

sidecarExt.description: File extension for the sidecar, without the dot, e.g. xml, csv, txt, jdf. Defaults to json for the JSON format and txt for a custom template. xml is sent as application/xml, csv as text/csv, anything else from a custom template as text/plain.

includeFullReport.description: Also deliver the complete preflight report JSON next to each print file (Business_Cards.report.json). Only takes effect when sidecar is true and the job ran a preflight.

emailParams.description: Email delivery: one message per job with a download link per file (files are never attached). Links go through FileCheck's download host and stay valid for linkExpiryHours. Sent from FileCheck's mail sender, or the account's own SMTP server when one is configured in settings.

to.description: Recipient address. Leave it out and the email goes to the job's customer email, i.e. the shopper who placed the order, not the print shop; set it to the shop's production inbox to notify the shop instead. The destination test needs either this or the caller's own address.

cc.description: One address to copy on every delivery email.

bcc.description: One address to blind-copy on every delivery email, e.g. an archive inbox.

replyTo.description: Where replies go. Defaults to FileCheck's sender address. Not editable in the dashboard; a later save from the dashboard editor drops it.

subject.description: Subject line. Tokens: {orderId}, {jobId}, {jobName}, {product}, {customer} (customer email), {name} (account holder's name). Default: "Your print files {orderId} are ready".

attachMetadata.description: Attach a JSON file with the order, product and per-file preflight metadata (order-<orderId>-metadata.json). Off when omitted; the dashboard turns it on for new email destinations.

includeMetadata.description: Add an order and preflight summary table (order, product, SKU, quantity, preflight verdict per file) under the download links in the default email body. Ignored when templateId supplies the body.

templateId.description: Id of one of the account's own email templates (Library > Emails) to use as the body instead of FileCheck's default. The template's HTML and text bodies take the subject tokens plus {links}. Not editable in the dashboard's destination editor; a later save from it drops this field.

s3Params.description: Amazon S3 hotfolder: each file is written as an object in the print shop's bucket. FileCheck writes either by assuming a role in the shop's AWS account (access role: the shop creates a role whose trust policy allows FileCheck's AWS account, from the destination setup action, with the condition sts:ExternalId = externalId, and grants it s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectAcl on arn:aws:s3:::<bucket>/<prefix>/*) or with its own credentials (access policy: the shop's bucket policy grants FileCheck's account those two actions).

bucket.description: Bucket name only (no s3:// and no path), e.g. acme-prepress-inbox.

region.description: The bucket's AWS region, e.g. us-east-1. Defaults to eu-central-1 (FileCheck's own region), so set it whenever the bucket lives elsewhere or writes will fail.

access.description: How FileCheck gets write access. role (recommended): assume roleArn with externalId. policy: the bucket policy grants FileCheck's AWS account directly; roleArn is then ignored. Omitted: behaves as role when roleArn is set and as policy when it is not.

roleArn.description: ARN of the IAM role in the shop's account that FileCheck assumes, e.g. arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/filecheck-delivery. Required with access role.

externalId.description: The secret-ish value the role's trust policy requires as sts:ExternalId, guarding against other FileCheck accounts using the same role. Generate a random, unguessable value (the dashboard uses fcx_ followed by 24 hex characters), give it to the shop's AWS admin for the trust policy, and never reuse it across shops. Changing it requires updating the role. Required with access role.

acl.description: Canned ACL set on each object. Omit it for the bucket default; buckets with ACLs disabled (the AWS default since 2023) reject any ACL except bucket-owner-full-control. With access policy, bucket-owner-full-control makes sure the shop owns the delivered files.

prefix.description: Key prefix (folder) inside the bucket; leading and trailing slashes are ignored. Without tokens, objects land at <prefix>/orders/<orderId>/<file> (or <prefix>/jobs/<jobId>/<file>). With any {token} the prefix is the whole key layout. Tokens: {orderId}, {jobId}, {jobName}, {sku}, {productId}, {product}, {itemId}, {quantity}, {fileId}, {customer}, {filename}, {basename}, {ext}, {n}, {date} (YYYYMMDD), {yyyy}, {mm}, {dd}, {rand}; values are made path-safe, empty tokens drop their folder level, and the filename is appended unless {filename} or {basename} is used. Example: "hotfolder/{date}/{orderId}".

webhookParams.description: Webhook delivery: one JSON POST per job to url, 10-second timeout, no retries. Body: { event: "job.delivered" ("destination.test" for a test), jobId, orderId, customerEmail, product { itemId, productId, sku, name, quantity }, files [ { name, mimeType, taskId, url } ], meta }. The file urls are signed download links valid for linkExpiryHours. Use this to reach Dropbox, Google Drive, Box or OneDrive through a Zapier or Make catch hook.

url.description: The endpoint that receives the POST. Use https: the body carries download links to the customer's files.

headerName.description: Name of one extra request header for authenticating the call, e.g. Authorization or X-Api-Key. Sent only when headerValue is set.

headerValue.description: Value of the headerName header, e.g. "Bearer abc123". Secret: send plaintext, it is encrypted on save and reads back as ********; the stored form is { "enc": "..." }.

includeLinks.description: Include the files array with download links. Set false to send only the job, order and product details.

meta.description: Free-form JSON object copied as-is into every payload as meta, e.g. { "source": "filecheck", "shop": "acme" }, for routing on the receiving side. Any keys are allowed.

sftpParams.description: SFTP hotfolder: files are uploaded over SSH, creating folders as needed. Authenticate with password or privateKey (at least one).

host.description: Server host name or IPv4 address only, e.g. sftp.printer.example (no sftp:// and no port).

password.description: Login password. Secret: send plaintext, it is encrypted on save and reads back as ********; the stored form is { "enc": "..." }.

privateKey.description: Private key for key-based login: the full text of an OpenSSH, PEM or PuTTY private key, line breaks included ("-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\n..."), never the public key. Secret: encrypted on save, reads back as ********; the stored form is { "enc": "..." }.

passphrase.description: Passphrase that unlocks privateKey, if the key is encrypted. Secret: encrypted on save, reads back as ********.

path.description: Folder on the server, measured from the server's root ("incoming" and "/incoming" both mean /incoming), created if missing. Without tokens, files land in <path>/orders/<orderId>/<file> (or <path>/jobs/<jobId>/<file>). With any {token} the path is the whole layout. Tokens: {orderId}, {jobId}, {jobName}, {sku}, {productId}, {product}, {itemId}, {quantity}, {fileId}, {customer}, {filename}, {basename}, {ext}, {n}, {date} (YYYYMMDD), {yyyy}, {mm}, {dd}, {rand}; values are made path-safe, empty tokens drop their folder level, and the filename is appended unless {filename} or {basename} is used. Example: "/hotfolder/{orderId}/{sku}".

ftpParams.description: FTP hotfolder: files are uploaded over FTP, or explicit FTPS when secure is true, creating folders as needed.

host.description: Server host name or IPv4 address only, e.g. ftp.printer.example (no ftp:// and no port).

username.description: Login user name. Omit only for an anonymous FTP server (logs in as anonymous).

password.description: Login password. Secret: send plaintext, it is encrypted on save and reads back as ********; the stored form is { "enc": "..." }.

secure.description: Use explicit FTPS (AUTH TLS on the normal port). Leave false for plain FTP; implicit FTPS on port 990 is not supported.

path.description: Folder relative to the directory the FTP login starts in, created if missing. Without tokens, files land in <path>/orders/<orderId>/<file> (or <path>/jobs/<jobId>/<file>). With any {token} the path is the whole layout. Tokens: {orderId}, {jobId}, {jobName}, {sku}, {productId}, {product}, {itemId}, {quantity}, {fileId}, {customer}, {filename}, {basename}, {ext}, {n}, {date} (YYYYMMDD), {yyyy}, {mm}, {dd}, {rand}; values are made path-safe, empty tokens drop their folder level, and the filename is appended unless {filename} or {basename} is used. Example: "/hotfolder/{orderId}/{sku}".

OptimizePreset.title: Optimize preset
OptimizePreset.description: A saved, named set of PDF optimizations (downsample or AI-upscale images, recompress, convert colors to CMYK/gray/RGB, outline text, flatten layers, thicken hairlines, strip junk, resize pages, set trim/crop boxes, add bleed, embed an output-intent ICC profile) that a job applies to the customer's PDF. Workflows point at it from an optimize step, workflow.streams[].steps[] { type: "optimize", config: { presetId } }, and rules from rule.accepts[].flow.optimize.presetId (when flow.optimize.enabled). The preset is read at run time, so edits apply to the next job. The proof sheet also takes its page size from pageResize and its ICC profile from outputIntent. Presets apply to PDFs only, including raster uploads after a Convert-to-PDF step; raster optimize ignores them. The stored shape is NOT the params shape of POST /jobs/optimize: here every group is an object with its own `enabled` switch and only groups with enabled true are applied (a group without enabled: true does nothing), scaleImages.targetRes is a single DPI number, and flattenLayers is { enabled }. Other keys in the optimize step's config, written in the POST /jobs/optimize params.pdf shape, replace the preset's group of the same name for that step. Groups run as: AI upscale and bleed fill first, then the DynaPDF pass (resize, boxes, conversion, compression, output intent).

title.description: Name shown in the dashboard's preset pickers, e.g. "Offset CMYK, 300 dpi, 3 mm bleed". The dashboard will not save a preset without one.

tags.description: Free-form labels for organising the Library. Not used at run time.

groupEnabled.description: Switch for this group: true applies it, false keeps the settings but skips it. Required, because a group without enabled: true does nothing.

bw.description: DPI for 1-bit black and white images.

scaleImages.description: Downsample images whose resolution is above targetRes, to shrink the file. Never increases resolution (that is upscaleImages).

targetRes.description: Target resolution in DPI that larger images are downsampled to, e.g. 300 for offset, 150 for large format. One number applies to color, gray and 1-bit images alike (the dashboard edits only this form); a { bw, gray, color } object sets channels separately. Images at or below targetRes are left alone.

minRes.description: Per-channel threshold in DPI: only images above it are downsampled. Defaults to targetRes + 1 per channel. Not editable in the dashboard; a later save there drops it.

skipMasked.description: Leave images that have a color mask untouched.

skipSizeCheck.description: Write the downsampled image even when it comes out larger than the original. Not editable in the dashboard; a later save there drops it.

upscaleImages.description: AI-upscale placed images whose effective resolution is below targetDpi (an external AI service, run before everything else; adds processing time per image). RGB, gray and indexed images only; CMYK and JPEG 2000 images are left as they are. Combined with scaleImages, keep targetDpi at or below scaleImages.targetRes, or images are upscaled and then immediately downsampled again.

targetDpi.description: Effective DPI every placed image should reach at its printed size.

maxScale.description: Largest enlargement factor per image; images needing more are enlarged to this and reported as still below target.

maxImages.description: Most images upscaled per document, worst DPI first; the rest are reported as skipped.

compression.description: Recompress image streams. Filters left out keep the optimizer's own choice. The dashboard starts new presets at ccitt4 / jpeg / jpeg with quality 80; jpeg and jpeg2000 are lossy, so prefer flate where print quality matters more than size.

bwFilter.description: Filter for 1-bit black and white images: flate (lossless), ccitt3 / ccitt4 (lossless fax), jbig2 (best for scanned text), lzw, runlength.

grayFilter.description: Filter for grayscale images: flate or lzw (lossless), jpeg or jpeg2000 (lossy).

colorFilter.description: Filter for color images: flate or lzw (lossless), jpeg or jpeg2000 (lossy).

jpegQuality.description: JPEG quality, 1 (smallest) to 100 (best). 80 to 90 is typical for print.

use1BitJBIG2.description: Recompress 1-bit images with JBIG2 (very compact for scanned text); images already in JBIG2 are skipped.

recompressJBIG2.description: Re-encode 1-bit images even when they are already JBIG2. Only with use1BitJBIG2.

colorConversion.description: Convert text, vector art and (with convertSpecialSpaces) images to one device color space, e.g. RGB uploads to CMYK for offset.

target.description: Color space to convert to: cmyk (press), rgb (screen or some digital presses) or gray (black-only jobs).

convertSpecialSpaces.description: Also convert images and Separation, DeviceN and NChannel colors (spot inks) unless listed in preserve. Off converts only text and vectors in ordinary color spaces; turn it on for a full conversion.

preserve.description: Color-space families to leave untouched: separation keeps spot inks (Pantone, white, varnish, cutter), separationAll keeps the All separation used for registration marks, deviceN and nchannel keep multi-ink builds, icc keeps ICC-based colors.

excludeColorSpaces.description: Named color spaces (e.g. "PANTONE 185 C", "Cutter") to exclude from, or limit, the conversion. Stored for the dashboard but not applied by the optimizer yet; use preserve to keep spot inks.

excludeMode.description: How excludeColorSpaces is read: exclude the listed spaces, or convert only them. Not applied by the optimizer yet.

replaceJpeg2000WithJpeg.description: Recompress converted JPEG 2000 images as JPEG (much faster, near-identical quality).

onOverprint.description: What to do with overprinting objects, whose appearance can change when converted. fail: stop the optimize step with an error (the dashboard's default for new presets; overprinting black text is common, so expect failures). skip: leave overprinting objects in their original color space. convert: convert them anyway. Omitted behaves as convert.

grayTo1Bit.description: Convert grayscale images to 1-bit black and white (compressed as JBIG2). For line art and scanned text only; destroys photos.

useOtsuFilter.description: Pick the black/white threshold per image with Otsu's method (better for scans).

textToOutlines.description: Convert text to vector outlines, so missing or unlicensed fonts cannot reflow on press. The result has no searchable text.

nonEmbeddedOnly.description: Outline only text set in fonts that are not embedded; embedded fonts stay as text.

flattenLayers.description: Flatten optional content (layers) into one visible layer, so hidden or print-only layers cannot surprise the press. An object, not a boolean.

hairlines.description: Thicken strokes thinner than minWidth so they do not break up or vanish on press.

minWidth.description: Minimum stroke width in points (1 pt = 1/72 inch = 0.353 mm). Typical: 0.25 for sheetfed offset, 0.5 for flexo, 0.75 to 1 for large format and screen printing.

ignoreZeroWidth.description: Leave zero-width strokes (drawn one device pixel wide) alone. Off by default because they are the most common hairline hazard.

zeroWidthOnly.description: Only widen zero-width strokes and leave thin non-zero strokes as designed.

strip.description: Remove non-printing objects to shrink or sanitize the file. Each switch defaults to off.

privateData.description: Remove application-private data (e.g. Illustrator or InDesign editing data).

invisiblePaths.description: Remove vector paths that draw nothing.

batesNumbers.description: Remove Bates numbering and its headers and footers.

headerFooter.description: Remove headers and footers added by PDF tools (not Bates numbers).

annotations.description: Drop all annotations (comments, sticky notes, links, stamps).

formFields.description: Drop interactive form fields (AcroForm and XFA).

javascript.description: Drop document JavaScript and JavaScript actions.

pageResize.description: Resize every page. Give a named format, or width and height in points, or scaleX/scaleY factors; the first of those present wins (format, then width/height, then factors). One scale computed from page 1 is applied to the whole document. Cannot be combined with bleed using fill none.

mode.description: How content meets a size target (format or width/height): scale keeps proportions and fits inside the target (may leave margins); stretch scales X and Y independently to fill it exactly (may distort). Ignored when only scaleX/scaleY are given.

format.description: Named paper size: A3, A4, A5, Letter, Legal or Tabloid, turned by orientation. Takes precedence over width/height and scale factors. null when not used.

orientation.description: Orientation applied to format. Ignored otherwise.

width.description: Target page width in points (1 pt = 1/72 inch, so points = mm x 2.8346; A4 is 595 x 842). Needs height. null when not used.

height.description: Target page height in points. Needs width. null when not used.

scaleX.description: Horizontal scale factor (1 = unchanged, 0.5 = half), used only when neither format nor width/height is set.

scaleY.description: Vertical scale factor, used only when neither format nor width/height is set. Defaults to scaleX.

boundingBoxes.description: Set the trim box and/or crop box of every page as margins inset from the page's media box, so one preset works for any page size. For adding bleed use the bleed group instead; with bleed fill mirror or scale the pages are rebuilt and a trim entry here is ignored.

entries.description: At most one entry per box (one trim, one crop).

boundingBox.description: One box, as margins in points measured inward from the media box edges.

box.description: Which page box to set: trim (the finished, cut size) or crop (the visible area in viewers).

source.description: Box the margins are measured from. Always "media"; required, an entry without it fails the optimize step.

top.description: Inset of the top edge in points (1 pt = 1/72 inch; 3 mm = 8.504 pt), positive inward.

bottom.description: Inset of the bottom edge in points, positive inward.

left.description: Inset of the left edge in points, positive inward.

right.description: Inset of the right edge in points, positive inward.

expand.description: Uniform change on all four sides in points, positive OUTWARD (opposite sign to the per-side insets); added to them.

page.description: 1-based page to apply to; null or omitted applies to every page.

bleed.description: Add bleed around the finished size. The page's trim box (or the whole page when it has none) is taken as the trim, required_mm is added beyond it, and the media, bleed and trim boxes are set. fill decides what goes into the new strip.

required_mm.description: Bleed in millimetres added on each selected edge, e.g. 3 (3.175 for 1/8 inch).

fill.description: How the new strip is filled. none: only the page boxes are set, so the artwork must already extend past the trim. mirror: edge artwork is reflected outward into the bleed (the dashboard's default for new presets). scale: page content is enlarged slightly so it overflows the trim. mirror and scale also flatten visible annotations into the artwork. With pageResize enabled, fill must be mirror or scale.

sides.description: Edges that get bleed: ["all"] (default) or any of top, right, bottom, left. Ignored for fill scale, which always grows every edge.

outputIntent.description: Embed an ICC profile as the PDF's output intent, declaring the printing condition the file is meant for (PDF/X workflows). Also sets the profile the proof is rendered with. Does not convert colors; use colorConversion for that.

profile.description: Bundled ICC profile. CMYK modern: fogra51 (PSO Coated v3), fogra52 (PSO Uncoated v3), gracol2013, swop2013. CMYK legacy coated: fogra39 (Coated FOGRA39), iso-coated-v2, iso-coated-v2-300, gracol2006, swop (US Web Coated SWOP v2). CMYK legacy uncoated: fogra29. Japan: japan-coated, japan-uncoated. Web offset: psr-lwc, psr-snp. RGB: srgb, adobe-rgb, display-p3. Gray: greyscale. Required when enabled; null otherwise.

condition.description: Free-text name of the printing condition, e.g. "Coated FOGRA39 (ISO 12647-2:2004)". Shown in the dashboard only; the embedded output intent comes from the profile alone.

ProductMap.title: Product mapping
ProductMap.description: Which workflow a product in your store uses. The storefront Element loads the mapped workflow on that product's page, and the workflow's intake rule decides which files the customer can upload. A product can use one workflow for every variant, or a different workflow per variant (for example one per size); a variant without its own workflow uses the product's. The id in the path is the product id as your store knows it (Shopify: the numeric product id). On WooCommerce, PrestaShop and OpenCart the product's workflow is set in the FileCheck plugin's product settings instead.

workflowId.description: The published workflow every variant uses unless it has its own. null when only variants are mapped.

title.description: The product title, shown in the dashboard's product list.

url.description: The product's storefront page, so the dashboard can link to where the upload form now appears.

variants.description: Per-variant workflows, keyed by the variant id as your store knows it (Shopify: the numeric variant id). Sending this replaces the whole set; leave it out to keep the stored one.

workflowId.description: The published workflow this variant uses; null to fall back to the product's.

title.description: The variant title (for example "A5 / Matte"), shown in the dashboard.

Profile.title: Profile
Profile.description: A preflight profile: the checks FileCheck runs on an uploaded file, each with its settings (target), how a failure is judged (severity) and whether it is repaired automatically. There are two kinds. A PDF profile (kind omitted or 'pdf') checks PDFs, and vector and office files once converted to PDF; its checks sit in the sections geometry (geom.*), color (color.*), text (text.*), images (image.*) and structure (struct.*). A raster profile (kind: 'raster') checks image uploads (JPEG, PNG, TIFF and so on) with the single section raster (raster.*). An upload rule points at profiles through rule.accepts[].preflight.profileId: pdf, vector and office accepts need a PDF profile, raster accepts a raster profile. A check runs only when both its section's enabled and its own enabled are true; everything omitted is off. Each check has a severity. reject: a failing file is rejected (shown as a warning instead when the upload rule's onFail is not reject). warn: it passes with a warning. ignore: the finding is recorded but never fails or warns. autofix: the customer is told FileCheck repairs it, and the finding is judged as reject when this file is beyond the repair; autofix is accepted only on checks that have a repair (their description says Autofix: …). Repairs run only in workflows with an autofix step, which repairs every failed check that has a repair whatever its severity, so to stop a repair disable the check. Units are in the field names: _mm millimetres, _pt points (1/72 in), _dpi or dpi pixels per inch, percent, _px pixels, _mb megabytes. Unknown check ids, a check in the wrong section and misspelled settings are refused.

title.description: Name shown in the dashboard and in the profile picker of upload rules, e.g. 'Business cards 85 x 55 mm'. Keep it under 45 characters, the dashboard editor's limit; the dashboard will not save a profile without one.

description.description: Note for the print shop: what the profile is for. Shown in the dashboard editor of PDF profiles; never shown to customers.

kind.description: 'raster' for an image profile; 'pdf' or omitted for a PDF profile. Decides which sections are valid: changing it on an existing profile means replacing its sections too, and upload rules pointing at it must match the new kind.

metadata.description: Legacy metadata carried by built-in catalog profiles.

kind.description: Legacy copy of kind. Must agree with kind; 'raster' here without kind: 'raster' is refused because the dashboard would open the profile as a PDF profile and drop its raster checks.

description.description: Catalog blurb of built-in profiles; not shown anywhere. Use description instead.

tags.description: Free-form labels for your own organisation, e.g. ['business-cards', 'cmyk']. Not shown to customers.

sections.description: The checks, grouped in sections keyed by section id. PDF profiles: geometry (geom.* checks), color (color.*), text (text.*), images (image.*), structure (struct.*) and page_rules (reserved, keep empty). Raster profiles: raster (raster.*). Each section is { enabled, rules: { <check id>: { enabled, severity, target, autofixStrategy } } }. To change one setting, PATCH only that path, e.g. { "sections": { "geometry": { "rules": { "geom.bleed.required": { "target": { "required_mm": 3 } } } } } }; when enabling a check, also send its section's enabled: true.

noTarget.description: This check has no settings: omit target, or send null or {}.

ruleEnabled.description: true runs this check; false or omitted leaves it off. Its section's enabled must also be true.

legacyMessage.description: Legacy free-text note stored by older dashboards. Not shown to customers (their messages come from FileCheck's built-in text for each check id); leave null or omit.

sectionEnabled.description: Must be true for any check in this section to run: the runtime skips the whole section otherwise, whatever the checks say. Keep it true exactly when at least one check is enabled, as the dashboard does; it is refused as false or missing while a check in the section is enabled.

geom.page_count.description: Number of pages. Fails when the count is not one of allowed (if set), or is below min or above max; every limit you set must hold. A page count chosen on the storefront product page replaces min and max for that order. No automatic repair.

id.description: The check id, 'geom.page_count'. Optional; must equal the key.

severity.description: reject, warn or ignore. Omitted = warn. autofix is refused: this check has no repair, and an autofix finding would promise the customer a fix that never happens.

autofixStrategy.description: Display label for the repair. No label exists for this check: leave it null or omit it.

target.description: Settings for this check. Omitted fields use the defaults described on each field.

min.description: Fewest pages accepted. null or omitted = no lower limit.

max.description: Most pages accepted. null or omitted = no upper limit.

allowed.description: Exact page counts accepted, e.g. [1, 2] for one- or two-sided. Empty or omitted = any count within min and max.

geom.page_size.description: Finished page size. Each page's trim size (its TrimBox when it has one, else the visible page) must match one of allowed within tolerance_mm, in either orientation. A page with no TrimBox that is an allowed size plus an even margin on every side is read as trim + bleed when geom.bleed.required asks for bleed on all sides. A size chosen on the storefront product page replaces allowed for that order. Autofix: rescales the document to the nearest allowed size when every page misses by no more than autofix_within_percent and all pages need the same size; with fit_mode on, fits each page onto the product size instead. A file beyond the repair is judged as reject.

id.description: The check id, 'geom.page_size'. Optional; must equal the key.

severity.description: reject, warn, ignore or autofix (FileCheck repairs it; judged as reject when this file is beyond the repair). Omitted = warn. Severity only decides how a failure is judged: a workflow autofix step repairs every failed check that has a repair, whatever its severity.

autofixStrategy.description: Display label for the repair, shown in the dashboard; the runtime picks the repair from the check id and ignores this field. Known labels: 'rescale-page'. null or omitted is fine.

target.description: Settings for this check. Omitted fields use the defaults described on each field.

allowed.description: Accepted finished (trim) sizes in millimetres, without bleed. Either orientation passes: 85 x 55 also accepts 55 x 85. US sizes in mm: 8.5 x 11 in = 215.9 x 279.4. Required (non-empty) when the check is enabled.

tolerance_mm.description: How far, in mm, each side may differ from an allowed size and still pass. Default 0.5.

autofix_within_percent.description: Near-miss rescale window, in percent of the size: the repair rescales only pages within this distance of an allowed size. Default 10; 0 is read as 10, so to keep the rescale from ever applying use a tiny value such as 0.1. Ignored when fit_mode is on.

fit_mode.description: Fit to product size, for files of any size. off (default): only the near-miss rescale. contain: scale the design to fit inside the product, whole design visible, gaps filled per fit_fill. cover: scale to fill the product, overflow cropped.

fit_fill.description: With fit_mode on: mirror (default) fills gaps and bleed by reflecting the artwork edges; white leaves gaps white and mirrors only the bleed where artwork meets the cut.

fit_max_scale.description: With fit_mode on: the largest enlargement factor, and its reciprocal the largest reduction. Default 2 (from half to double size); files needing more are not repaired.

geom.bleed.required.description: Bleed: how far the bleed area (BleedBox, else the page edge) extends past the trim (TrimBox) on each checked edge, which must be required_mm plus or minus tolerance_mm. Pages without a TrimBox are judged by their BleedBox margins, or read as trim + bleed when geom.page_size allows the inner size. Too much bleed fails too. Autofix: rebuilds the page boxes to exactly required_mm of bleed and fills the new strip per fill. Not offered for a document whose pages disagree.
