geom.bleed.content_coverage.description: Artwork in the bleed: whether the printed content really extends required_mm past the trim (or reaches the page edge when there is no TrimBox), so no white slivers show after cutting. Blank pages are skipped; crop marks outside the trim can hide a bare edge. Autofix: adds bleed by mirroring or scaling the edge artwork. When geom.bleed.required fails on the same file one bleed pass runs and the first fill seen wins (normally geom.bleed.required's), so give that check a fill of mirror or scale too.

severity.description: reject, warn, ignore or autofix (FileCheck repairs it; judged as reject when this file is beyond the repair). Omitted = warn. Severity only decides how a failure is judged: a workflow autofix step repairs every failed check that has a repair, whatever its severity.

autofixStrategy.description: Display label for the repair, shown in the dashboard; the runtime picks the repair from the check id and ignores this field. Known labels: 'remove-alpha', 'flatten-background'. null or omitted is fine.

target.description: Settings for this check. Omitted fields use the defaults described on each field.

allowed.description: false flags transparent images; true accepts them. Required when the check is enabled.

background.description: Repair: colour the image is flattened onto, as #rrggbb. Default #ffffff (white).

raster.background_removal.description: Background removal, a requested transform rather than a defect: with remove true, every upload that has no transparency yet gets its background removed by AI. Severity must be autofix. Autofix: removes the background with AI.

id.description: The check id, 'raster.background_removal'. Optional; must equal the key.

severity.description: Must be 'autofix': reject, warn, ignore or autofix (FileCheck repairs it; judged as reject when this file is beyond the repair). Omitted = warn. Severity only decides how a failure is judged: a workflow autofix step repairs every failed check that has a repair, whatever its severity.

autofixStrategy.description: Display label for the repair, shown in the dashboard; the runtime picks the repair from the check id and ignores this field. Known labels: 'remove-bg'. null or omitted is fine.

target.description: Settings for this check. Omitted fields use the defaults described on each field.

remove.description: true to remove backgrounds. Required (true) when the check is enabled.

raster.max_file_size.description: File size: fails when the image file is larger than max_mb megabytes. No automatic repair.

id.description: The check id, 'raster.max_file_size'. Optional; must equal the key.

severity.description: reject, warn or ignore. Omitted = warn. autofix is refused: this check has no repair, and an autofix finding would promise the customer a fix that never happens.

autofixStrategy.description: Display label for the repair. No label exists for this check: leave it null or omit it.

target.description: Settings for this check. Omitted fields use the defaults described on each field.

max_mb.description: Largest file accepted, in MB (1 MB = 1,048,576 bytes). Required when the check is enabled.

raster.icc_profile_required.description: Embedded colour profile: with 'any', fails when the image has no embedded ICC profile; with an alias, fails unless that exact profile is embedded. Autofix: embeds expected_profile_name and converts the pixels to it; 'any' embeds fogra39, a CMYK profile, so an RGB photo becomes CMYK.

id.description: The check id, 'raster.icc_profile_required'. Optional; must equal the key.

severity.description: reject, warn, ignore or autofix (FileCheck repairs it; judged as reject when this file is beyond the repair). Omitted = warn. Severity only decides how a failure is judged: a workflow autofix step repairs every failed check that has a repair, whatever its severity.

autofixStrategy.description: Display label for the repair. No label exists for this check: leave it null or omit it.

target.description: Settings for this check. Omitted fields use the defaults described on each field.

expected_profile_name.description: 'any' or the ICC alias the image must carry. Required when the check is enabled. FileCheck ICC aliases: fogra39 (Coated FOGRA39), fogra51 (PSO Coated v3), fogra52 (PSO Uncoated v3), fogra29 (Uncoated FOGRA29), iso-coated-v2, iso-coated-v2-300 (300 % ink cap), gracol2013, gracol2006, swop2013, swop (US Web Coated SWOP v2), japan-coated, japan-uncoated, psr-lwc, psr-snp (newsprint), srgb, adobe-rgb, display-p3, greyscale.

raster.aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio: fails when the image's width divided by height is further than tolerance from every ratio in ratio, in either orientation. Autofix: pads the image (letterbox or pillarbox, nothing cropped) to the nearest allowed ratio, with tolerance 0.02 when none is set.

id.description: The check id, 'raster.aspect_ratio'. Optional; must equal the key.

severity.description: reject, warn, ignore or autofix (FileCheck repairs it; judged as reject when this file is beyond the repair). Omitted = warn. Severity only decides how a failure is judged: a workflow autofix step repairs every failed check that has a repair, whatever its severity.

autofixStrategy.description: Display label for the repair, shown in the dashboard; the runtime picks the repair from the check id and ignores this field. Known labels: 'crop'. null or omitted is fine.

target.description: Settings for this check. Omitted fields use the defaults described on each field.

ratio.description: Accepted ratios, each as a string 'W:H' (also 'W/H' or 'WxH'), e.g. ['3:2', '4:3'], or a number = width divided by height (1.5). Either orientation passes. A list of two whole numbers such as [3, 2] means the ratios 3:1 and 2:1, not 3:2, and is refused; [1, 1] (square) is fine. Required (non-empty) when the check is enabled.

tolerance.description: Allowed difference between the image's width/height and a ratio, e.g. 0.02. Omitted = exact match.

raster.stitch_set.description: Stitch several uploads into one image. NOT IMPLEMENTED: the check never reports and nothing is stitched. Autofix: none in practice (the check never fails).

id.description: The check id, 'raster.stitch_set'. Optional; must equal the key.

severity.description: reject, warn, ignore or autofix (FileCheck repairs it; judged as reject when this file is beyond the repair). Omitted = warn. Severity only decides how a failure is judged: a workflow autofix step repairs every failed check that has a repair, whatever its severity.

autofixStrategy.description: Display label for the repair, shown in the dashboard; the runtime picks the repair from the check id and ignores this field. Known labels: 'stitch'. null or omitted is fine.

target.description: Settings for this check. Omitted fields use the defaults described on each field.

raster.tac.description: Total ink of the image once converted to CMYK: fails when any pixel's cyan + magenta + yellow + black exceeds max_percent. Autofix: converts the image to CMYK through icc_alias, whose gamut mapping caps the ink.

id.description: The check id, 'raster.tac'. Optional; must equal the key.

severity.description: reject, warn, ignore or autofix (FileCheck repairs it; judged as reject when this file is beyond the repair). Omitted = warn. Severity only decides how a failure is judged: a workflow autofix step repairs every failed check that has a repair, whatever its severity.

autofixStrategy.description: Display label for the repair, shown in the dashboard; the runtime picks the repair from the check id and ignores this field. Known labels: 'icc-convert'. null or omitted is fine.

target.description: Settings for this check. Omitted fields use the defaults described on each field.

max_percent.description: Maximum total ink in percent. Default 300.

icc_alias.description: Repair: CMYK ICC profile used for the conversion. '' or omitted = iso-coated-v2-300 (300 % cap); e.g. fogra29 for uncoated stock. FileCheck ICC aliases: fogra39 (Coated FOGRA39), fogra51 (PSO Coated v3), fogra52 (PSO Uncoated v3), fogra29 (Uncoated FOGRA29), iso-coated-v2, iso-coated-v2-300 (300 % ink cap), gracol2013, gracol2006, swop2013, swop (US Web Coated SWOP v2), japan-coated, japan-uncoated, psr-lwc, psr-snp (newsprint), srgb, adobe-rgb, display-p3, greyscale.

section.raster.description: Checks on an uploaded image file (JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP and so on). Check ids start with 'raster.'.

id.description: The section id, 'raster'. Optional; must equal the key.

title.description: Display title in the dashboard, e.g. 'Raster Checks'. Cosmetic.

rules.description: The checks of this section, keyed by check id: raster.format, raster.min_dimensions_px, raster.max_dimensions_px, raster.effective_dpi, raster.colorspace, raster.bit_depth, raster.transparency, raster.background_removal, raster.max_file_size, raster.icc_profile_required, raster.aspect_ratio, raster.stitch_set, raster.tac. Any other key is refused. Omitted checks are off.

section.page_rules.description: Reserved for per-page overrides, which are not evaluated yet. The dashboard saves it empty: keep rules {} and entries [], or omit the section.

id.description: The section id, 'page_rules'.

enabled.description: Has no effect; the dashboard saves false.

entries.description: Always []: per-page overrides are not supported yet.

pdfSections.description: Sections of a PDF profile. Omitted sections are off.

rasterSections.description: Sections of a raster profile: only raster.

Rule.title: Rule
Rule.description: An upload rule (intake rule): the contract for what a customer may upload for one product and how each file is judged at upload time, while the customer waits. A workflow points at exactly one rule through workflow.intake.ruleId, and many workflows can share a rule. For each uploaded file FileCheck detects the real type from the file's bytes, picks the matching entry in `accepts` (exact MIME type first, then the first entry of the same kind that is not mimeTypesStrict), optionally converts it to PDF, preflights it against the preflight profile that entry names (accepts[].preflight.profileId; profiles hold the checks and thresholds, a rule only points at them), and turns a failing result into reject / accept-with-warnings / manual-review through that entry's onFail. Accepted files then feed the workflow stream for their kind (pdf, raster or other). `cardinality` says how many files the product needs. A rule does no downstream processing: autofix, optimize, imposition, proofing and delivery are configured on the workflow.

title.description: Name of the rule in the dashboard library and in workflow pickers, e.g. "Business Card — Front & Back". Keep it under 60 characters, the dashboard editor's limit.

description.description: Note for the print shop's dashboard: which product this rule is for and which profile it pairs with. Never shown to customers.

instructions.description: Short instruction shown to the customer in the upload widget, e.g. "Upload a print-ready PDF with 3 mm bleed on all sides." Plain text only: the widget renders it as HTML in slot mode, so angle brackets are refused.

tags.description: Free labels for finding the rule in the dashboard library (e.g. "pdf", "business-card"). No effect on uploads.

cardinality.description: How many files one order of this product needs: either a count range (min and max) or named slots (one labelled upload per slot, e.g. Front and Back). Omit it for exactly one file. A product page can override min and max per order through the job's fileCount context.

min.description: Fewest accepted files before the job leaves intake and the widget lets the customer continue. Required unless slots are set (then ignored). To let a customer skip uploading altogether use uploadOptional; min 0 alone does not do that.

max.description: Most files the customer may upload; the widget stops offering uploads at this count. Must be at least min (not checked here: with max below min the widget can never be satisfied). Required unless slots are set (then ignored). There is no unlimited value, because the widget reads a missing max as 1, so set a generous number such as 50.

slots.description: Named upload slots in order, e.g. ["Front", "Back"]. When non-empty the customer gets one labelled upload area per slot, exactly that many files are required, min and max are ignored, and each file keeps its slot name (proofs are shown in slot order). Empty means count-range mode.

accepts.description: The file types this product takes, normally one entry per kind (the dashboard allows only one), each with its own MIME list, size limit, PDF conversion, preflight profile and failure policy. For an upload, the first entry whose mimeTypes lists the file's detected MIME type wins; failing that, the first entry of the file's kind that is not mimeTypesStrict. A file no entry matches is refused by the widget when rejectUnknownTypes is true, but one sent through the API is stored unchecked, so cover every kind you expect.

rejectUnknownTypes.description: When true the upload widget refuses files that match no accepts entry; when false it lets them through and they are stored unchecked. Only the widget reads this: files submitted through the API that match no entry are always taken unchecked.

maxTotalSize.description: Intended cap on the combined size of one order's files, in bytes. Stored and shown in the dashboard but not enforced anywhere today; use accepts[].maxSize for a limit that works. Omit or null for none.

uploadOptional.description: When true a customer who uploads nothing may continue: the widget's checkout gate opens with zero files. Once any file is uploaded, cardinality and onFail apply as usual, and a rejected file still blocks.

channels.description: Reserved for limiting the rule to submission channels (client = the storefront widget, api, admin, store). Not enforced today: leave it empty, which means all channels.

ui.description: Look-and-feel overrides for the storefront upload widget while it shows this rule. A key set here overrides the account default and is overridden by the host page; leave a key out to inherit. Never affects which files are accepted.

title.description: Heading shown at the top of the widget.

theme.description: Colour scheme: light, dark, or system (follow the shopper's device setting).

accent.description: Accent colour override, e.g. #0a7cff; null inherits the account's brand colour.

locale.description: BCP-47 language tag for the widget's text, e.g. de or fr-CA; null follows the host page.

layout.description: Hint to the host page's SDK on how to present the widget.

showHeader.description: Show the title and subtitle block.

showHelp.description: Show the help area with helpText.

helpText.description: Help text shown when showHelp is true.

submitLabel.description: Label for the host page's continue button once the upload is ready (the host renders the button).

autoSubmit.description: When true the host page moves on by itself as soon as the upload is ready, without a click.

branding.description: Which branding the widget shows: the account's (domain), none, or custom.

resultsDisplay.description: full shows each file's findings inline; list shows a compact, selectable file list for pairing with a separate report element.

proofDetails.description: How the proof dialog opens: collapsed (the print first, findings behind a summary button) or expanded (findings panel open).

mimeType.description: A lowercase MIME type exactly as FileCheck's detection reports it, e.g. application/pdf, image/jpeg (never image/jpg), image/tiff (never image/tif).

accept.description: One accepted file kind: which files it matches and how each one is checked and judged on upload.

kind.description: The file family this entry handles, matched against the type FileCheck detects from the bytes. pdf: PDF (and PDF-based .ai). raster: JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP, HEIC, AVIF, GIF, BMP. vector: SVG, EPS/PostScript. office: Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OpenDocument files. archive: ZIP. other: fonts and anything else. Only pdf and raster can be preflighted as uploaded; vector and office need convertToPdf first; archive and other are stored as-is with no checks.

mimeTypes.description: MIME types this entry claims; each must belong to the entry's kind. Unless mimeTypesStrict is true the list does not narrow anything: every file of the kind is still accepted through the kind fallback and the widget offers the whole kind. For kind other the list is the only way the widget recognises a file, so it must not be empty.

mimeTypesStrict.description: When true the mimeTypes list is authoritative: a file of this kind whose MIME type is not listed is refused, by the widget and by the server, e.g. raster with ["image/jpeg", "image/tiff"] refuses PNG. Leave false to take every file of the kind. Needs a non-empty mimeTypes.

extensions.description: File extensions for display, lowercase with a leading dot, e.g. [".pdf"]. Informational only: nothing matches uploads by extension, and the widget builds its file picker from mimeTypes.

maxSize.description: Largest single file this entry takes, in bytes (50 MB = 52428800). Enforced by the upload widget before upload; files sent through the API are not checked against it. Omit or null for no limit.

convertToPdf.description: Vector and office entries only: convert each upload to PDF on arrival, so it can be preflighted against a PDF profile and feeds the workflow's pdf stream. Without it these files are stored as-is and feed the other stream. Must be false for pdf, raster, archive and other entries.

preflight.description: The check run on each file of this entry while the customer waits. Off unless enabled is sent as true, and then it needs a profileId. Possible for pdf and raster entries, and for vector and office entries with convertToPdf true; never for archive or other.

enabled.description: Run the preflight check. Send it explicitly; with false the file is accepted without a check.

profileId.description: What to check against: the id of a preflight profile record (from GET /profiles, usually profile_...), or a built-in conformance validation: 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 2u, 3a, 3b, 3u, 4, 4e, 4f (PDF/A) or ua1, ua2 (PDF/UA). The profile's kind must match the entry: pdf entries, and vector or office entries with convertToPdf, take a PDF profile or a validation id; raster entries take a raster profile. Required when enabled; ignored when not.

onFail.description: What a failing preflight (or a failed PDF conversion) means for the file. reject: not accepted; the widget blocks the customer until they replace it and the job waits at intake. accept_with_warnings: accepted anyway; the profile's reject-level findings show as warnings and the workflow goes ahead. manual_review: the widget lets the customer continue and marks the file as awaiting review with findings as warnings, but the server does not count the file as accepted, so the workflow waits at intake until the print shop deals with it. A file FileCheck cannot open is rejected under every policy.

Settings.title: Storefront settings
Settings.description: How the FileCheck Element (the upload form on your product pages) appears and behaves in your store. Every setting has a default; in a PATCH, null puts a setting back to it. Custom JS and CSS, which run code in your store, can only be changed in the dashboard.

presentation.description: inline: the upload form sits on the product page. dialog: an "Upload Files" button opens the form in a popup.

mountSelector.description: CSS selector of the element the upload form (or, in dialog mode, its button) is placed into, used when the page has no element with id fc-inline. Empty: rely on #fc-inline (the Shopify app block and the cart plugins add it).

moveMountBefore.description: Dialog mode only: CSS selector of an element the "Upload Files" button is inserted before (for example the quantity field). Empty: the button goes into #fc-inline, then mountSelector, then next to the add-to-cart button.

cartButtonSelector.description: CSS selector(s) for the add-to-cart button, added to the built-in list. The Element keeps that button disabled until the customer's files are accepted, so set this when a theme's button isn't found.

elementTheme.description: The upload form's colour theme. system follows the shopper's device setting.

proofDetails.description: How the proof opens for the customer. collapsed: the print first, with the issues behind a summary button. expanded: the list of issues open beside it.

galleryProof.description: Show the product proof (3D model, folded leaflet, sheet, booklet) in place of the product page's own image gallery once every uploaded file has its proof. Off keeps the proof in the popup only.

gallerySelector.description: CSS selector of the product gallery's container, for themes whose gallery the built-in selectors miss. Only used with galleryProof.

Webhook.title: Webhook
Webhook.description: An HTTPS endpoint FileCheck calls when events happen on your account: jobs created, completed or delivered, proofs ready or approved, settings changed, credits running low. Each call is a JSON POST signed with X-FileCheck-Signature (the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with your Auth Key). Delivery is attempted once; the webhook records the last status it got.

url.description: The HTTPS URL that receives the POSTs.

events.description: The event keys this webhook receives, from GET /webhook-events (for example job.completed, proof.ready).

headers.description: Extra request headers sent with every call, such as an Authorization header your endpoint checks. Values are write-only: they read back as ********.

description.description: A note for yourself: what the endpoint is for.

Workflow.title: Workflow
Workflow.description: A workflow is the fulfilment pipeline for a product: what happens to a customer's upload from the moment it is dropped on the product page until the print-ready file reaches the shop. Intake runs first, while the customer waits: it points at an upload rule (which file kinds, how many files or slots, and per kind the preflight profile that checks them and whether a failing file is rejected). When the trigger fires (order placed, upload accepted, proof approved or a manual run), each accepted file runs the stream for its kind (autofix, convert an image to PDF, optimize with a preset, split pages); then merge can combine the files, and delivery sends the result to the account's destinations. Proofing optionally shows the customer a soft proof at the end of intake, and can hold the job until they approve it. Rules, preflight profiles, optimize presets, destinations and scenes are separate records referenced by id; product mappings and the embedded upload widget point at a workflow by its id. A job copies the workflow when it is created; jobs that already hold files keep the version they started with. A minimal create body is { "title", "intake": { "ruleId" } } plus one stream per file kind the rule accepts; without streams files are delivered as they left intake.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this record format. Always 1; can be left out.

title.description: Name shown in the dashboard, usually the product it serves (for example "Business cards 85 × 55 mm"). The dashboard's title editor takes up to 40 characters and will not save a workflow without one.

description.description: Internal note shown under the title in the dashboard. Customers never see it.

tags.description: Free-form labels for organising workflows (the spec importer adds "imported" and the product type). No effect on processing.

trigger.description: When processing after intake (streams, then merge and delivery) starts for a job whose files have passed intake. Until it fires, nothing after intake runs. "order_placed" (default): when the customer checks out in a connected cart and the order is linked to the job; the customer can still replace files until then, so use it on product pages. "on_accept": immediately, once the job holds enough accepted files for the rule's minimum file count; files are locked from then on. "proof_approval": when the customer approves the soft proof in the upload widget; needs proofing.enabled true. "manual": only when someone runs the job from the dashboard. Any job can also be run manually from the dashboard whatever its trigger.

intake.description: The upload stage. Runs for every uploaded file as soon as it arrives, whatever the trigger: checks the file against the upload rule and its preflight profile, and makes the soft proof when proofing is enabled.

ruleId.description: Id of the upload rule (GET /rules): the accepted file kinds and MIME types, the number of files or named slots, and per kind the preflight profile and onFail policy that decides whether a failing file is rejected. The upload widget will not load a workflow without a rule. The rule's accepted kinds decide which streams this workflow needs.

onError.description: Stored for the dashboard and not read by the pipeline: whether a failing file blocks the job is set per kind by the rule's onFail. Only "halt" is accepted.

enabled.description: Intake always runs and cannot be switched off. Always true.

kind.description: The file kind this stream processes, after intake: "pdf" for PDF uploads and for vector or office files the rule converts to PDF at intake (accept entry convertToPdf true); "raster" for JPEG, PNG, TIFF and other images; "other" for everything else (archives, fonts, vector or office files kept as they are), which no step can process.

type.description: What the step does. "autofix": applies the fixes the intake preflight planned for this file (the profile checks with severity "autofix": add bleed, convert to CMYK, upscale low-resolution images and so on); it is skipped when intake ran no preflight or found nothing to fix. If the upload rule already autofixes at intake (accept entry autofix on, without repreflight), keep this step disabled or the same fixes are applied a second time. "convert" (raster stream only): places the image on a new PDF page sized by config.dimension. "optimize": runs an optimize preset (config.presetId) over the PDF; on the raster stream it needs an enabled convert step before it, since it works on the converted PDF. "split_pages" (pdf stream only): writes one single-page PDF per page as extra outputs; the file that is delivered and downloaded stays the unsplit PDF.

enabled.description: false keeps the step and its settings in the workflow without running it. The dashboard lists every allowed step for a stream and switches them on and off this way.

onError.description: What a crash in this step does. "halt" (default): the file ends in error, which puts the whole job in error, so nothing is merged or delivered. "continue": the failure is recorded as a warning on the file and the job carries on with the file as it was before this step.

config.description: Settings for this step type: autofix {}, convert { format, dimension, outputIntent, dpi }, optimize { presetId }, split_pages {}.
Autofix takes no settings: it applies exactly the fixes the intake preflight planned for the file, as defined by the checks with severity "autofix" in the preflight profile. Send {}.
How the image becomes a PDF page.

format.description: Target format. Only "pdf" exists; it is what lets the following optimize step treat the file as a PDF.

dimension.description: Page the image is placed on, in millimetres. The image is scaled to fit inside the whole page (trim plus bleed), keeping its proportions, centred; if its proportions differ from the page the rest stays white. While the step is enabled, the page size (trim plus bleed) is also the print size used to judge a raster upload's effective DPI when the preflight profile sets none, and the sheet the soft proof is drawn on. Omit dimension to size the page from the image's pixels at dpi.

width.description: Finished (trim) width of the product in millimetres, without bleed. Example: 85 for an 85 × 55 mm business card.

height.description: Finished (trim) height of the product in millimetres, without bleed.

bleed.description: Bleed added outside the trim on each side, in millimetres: the page becomes trim + bleed and gets an explicit TrimBox (finished size) and BleedBox. Set it when customers upload images that already include bleed. For trim-sized images leave it out and let an optimize preset with a bleed group mirror-fill the bleed instead.

top.description: Top side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

bottom.description: Bottom side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

left.description: Left side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

right.description: Right side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

crop.description: Advanced: CropBox insets in millimetres, measured inward from the final page edge. Usually omitted.

top.description: Top side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

bottom.description: Bottom side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

left.description: Left side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

right.description: Right side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

trim.description: Advanced: TrimBox insets in millimetres, measured inward from the final page edge; when any side is set it replaces the TrimBox derived from bleed. Usually omitted.

top.description: Top side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

bottom.description: Bottom side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

left.description: Left side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

right.description: Right side, in millimetres. Missing sides count as 0.

matchOrientation.description: true (default): turn the page to the image's orientation, so a size set up portrait also takes landscape images (bleed and insets turn with it). false: always use width × height as given.

outputIntent.description: ICC profile to embed as the PDF's output intent, by bundled file name (for example "cmyk-fogra39.icc" or "cmyk-fogra39"). Short aliases such as "fogra39" are not resolved by the conversion. A profile the conversion cannot load is skipped without failing the step, so when the intent must be in the file, set it in the optimize preset's output-intent group instead. Also used as the colour profile the soft proof simulates.

dpi.description: Pixels per inch used to size the page from the image when dimension is not set (page = pixels ÷ dpi). Default 300. Ignored when dimension is set.

presetId.description: Id of the optimize preset to apply (GET /optimize-presets): image downsampling and compression, colour conversion, page resize, bleed, hairlines, output intent and so on, as configured on the preset. Required whenever the step is enabled.

config.description: Split pages takes no settings. Send {}.

steps.description: Steps run on each file of this kind, in this order, each on the previous step's output. Allowed types, in the order they must appear: pdf: autofix, optimize, split_pages. raster: autofix, convert, optimize. other: none. Each type at most once; leaving types out is fine. An empty list, or one with no enabled step, means files of this kind are delivered as they left intake.

streams.description: Per-file processing that runs after the trigger fires, one stream per file kind. After intake every accepted file is routed by kind: PDFs, and vector or office files the rule converts to PDF, go to the "pdf" stream; images go to the "raster" stream; anything else goes to "other". Add a stream for each kind the upload rule accepts, at most one per kind. A file whose kind has no stream is not processed and is delivered as it left intake. Named slots (Front, Back, …) do not get streams of their own: every file of a kind runs the same steps. Default [] (no processing).

merge.description: What happens to the job's files once every file has finished its stream. Runs once per job; a merged file replaces the individual files in delivery and in the job's deliverables (downloads, GET /jobs/{id}).

mode.description: "none" (default): files stay separate and are delivered one by one. "merge_pdf": all of the job's files are concatenated into one PDF in the order they were added to the job (slot names such as Front/Back do not affect the order); needs at least two files, and every file must be a PDF by the end of its stream, so the raster stream needs an enabled convert step and there must be no "other" stream. A merge that fails stops the job before its webhook and delivery. "zip": all files are bundled into one ZIP archive.

config.description: Mode settings: none {}, merge_pdf { order }, zip { names, order, zipName }.

onError.description: Stored for the dashboard; a failed merge always stops the job before delivery. Only "halt" is accepted.

enabled.description: false skips the merge whatever the mode. Default true.

order.description: Advanced: a permutation of the job's file positions (0-based, in the order the files were added to the job), listing every file exactly once. If a job has a different number of files than the list, the merge fails and the job is never delivered, so only use it when the upload rule fixes the file count (min equals max). Omit to keep the order the files were added.

names.description: File names to use inside the ZIP, by file position (the order the files were added to the job). Missing entries fall back to the stored file name, which is an internal id; duplicates get _2, _3 suffixes. With order set, names must have one entry per file.

order.description: Advanced: a permutation of the job's file positions (0-based, in the order the files were added to the job), listing every file exactly once. If a job has a different number of files than the list, the merge fails and the job is never delivered, so only use it when the upload rule fixes the file count (min equals max). Omit to keep the order the files were added.

zipName.description: Name for the archive itself (".zip" is added when it has no extension). Delivered files are named after the product or job, so this mostly shows in storage.

finalize.description: Reserved for steps after merge (imposition, export). None are implemented, so it must be empty.

proofing.description: Soft proof: a colour-managed preview of each uploaded file, drawn on the print sheet with bleed and cut marks and showing the fixes autofix will make, shown to the customer in the upload widget at the end of intake. With trigger "proof_approval" the job waits until the customer approves it; with any other trigger it is for information only.

id.description: Opaque id the dashboard stamps on this block. Optional; no effect.

enabled.description: Make a proof of every file at the end of intake. Default false. Must be true when trigger is "proof_approval".

type.description: Proof style. Only "basic" (rendered page previews) exists.

timing.description: When the proof is made. Only "after_intake" is implemented: after the file passes intake, before the trigger fires. Later points (after streams, after merge) are reserved and would produce no proof.

requireApproval.description: Informational only: whether the job waits for the customer's approval is decided by trigger "proof_approval", not by this flag.

previewer.description: What the customer approves on: the flat pages, or the proofed pages shown on a product scene.

kind.description: "pages" (default): flat page previews. "scene": the proofed pages shown on the 3D model, folded leaflet or booklet named by sceneId.

sceneId.description: Id of a scene from the scene library (the account's own or the built-in catalog): a 3D model, fold or flipbook the proofed pages are wrapped onto. Required when kind is "scene"; not allowed with "pages".

config.description: Advanced overrides for the proof render. Normally empty: the sheet, bleed and colour profile are inferred from the stream's optimize preset (pdf) or convert dimension (raster), falling back to the intake preflight profile.

iccProfile.description: Printing condition the proof simulates, replacing the inferred one: an alias such as "fogra39", "fogra51", "gracol2013", "swop2013", "srgb" or "greyscale", or a bundled ICC file name.

format.description: Image format of the proof pages. Default "webp".

quality.description: Compression quality of the proof images, 1 to 100. Default 91.

maxEdge.description: Longest side of a proof image in pixels. Default 1200.

sheet.description: Advanced: the print sheet each proof page is drawn on, replacing the inferred one (from the optimize preset's page size and bleed on the pdf stream, the convert dimension on the raster stream, else the preflight profile's page size and bleed). Omit unless the inference is wrong.

sizes.description: For products sold in several sizes: each page is proofed on the listed size nearest to it instead of on size.

bleed.description: Bleed shown around the trim, in millimetres. Default 0.

safeZone.description: Safety margin drawn inside the trim, in millimetres. Default 0.

fitTo.description: Fit the artwork to the trim (default) or to the full sheet including bleed.

fit.description: "contain" (default) shows the whole artwork inside the trim; "cover" fills the trim and crops the overflow.

dpi.description: Render resolution of the sheet in pixels per inch. Default 150; targetEdge wins when both are set.

targetEdge.description: Longest side of the rendered sheet in pixels, bleed included. Inferred sheets use 1200.

cutMarks.description: Draw corner cut marks and the dashed trim line. Default true.

watermark.description: Overlay a "proof" watermark band. Default false for a sheet given here (inferred sheets ask for one); it can also be switched off platform-wide.

matchOrientation.description: Turn the sheet to the artwork's orientation. Default true.

tags.description: Free-form labels. No effect.

optionSet.description: Customer-facing option fields (paper, sides, quantity and so on) meant to be shown next to the upload. Reserved: nothing reads it yet; the upload widget does not show it and jobs ignore it. Leave it disabled; product options belong in the store.

id.description: Opaque id the dashboard stamps on this block. Optional; no effect.

enabled.description: Has no effect yet. Default false.

key.description: Stable identifier, unique within the option set; dependsOn refers to it.

type.description: Widget: select (dropdown), radio, swatch, sides, binding, grommet, toggle, number, text, or note (read-only text).

value.description: Value recorded when the customer picks this choice.

label.description: Text shown for the choice. Defaults to the value.

swatch.description: Colour or material swatch for swatch fields.

priceHint.description: Cosmetic price note such as "+€2.00"; never used to price anything.

config.description: Free-form widget settings for this choice; any keys.

choices.description: Choices for select, radio, swatch, sides, binding and grommet fields.

unit.description: Unit label shown next to the value, such as "copies" or "mm".

key.description: Key of the field this one depends on.

in.description: Values of that field for which this one is shown.

dependsOn.description: Show this field only when another field has one of the listed values.

source.description: Fill the value from the uploaded file instead of asking: page_count, color_count, width, height or color_space.

preflightLink.description: Preflight concern this option relates to, such as "bleed" or "even_pages".

config.description: Free-form widget settings for this field; any keys.

fields.description: The option fields, in display order.

tags.description: Free-form labels. No effect.

delivery.description: Where the finished print files go when a job completes successfully (after streams and merge). Every destination receives the job's final files: the merged PDF or ZIP when merge made one, otherwise each file as its stream left it (the original upload when no step changed it). Jobs that end in error are not delivered.

enabled.description: true (default when delivery is sent): deliver to every listed destination. false: keep the list but deliver nothing.

destinationIds.description: Ids of delivery destinations (GET /destinations): email, S3, webhook, SFTP or FTP targets that hold their own credentials, paths and sidecar settings. Destinations that are disabled or deleted when a job finishes are skipped. Empty means nothing is delivered.

ui.description: Display settings for the dashboard and the upload widget. Free-form: unknown keys are kept as they are.

units.description: Unit for sizes shown to customers and in reports for jobs of this workflow; overrides the account default (millimetres when neither is set).

tags.description: Short labels shown on the workflow's card in the dashboard, for example ["2 × PDF", "85 × 55 mm"]; the description is shown when there are none.

id.description: The record id.

customized.description: Your own copy of a built-in record, under the same id. Revert drops it.

draft.description: Present and true on an unpublished draft.

draftExpiresAt.description: When an unpublished draft is deleted.

DestinationTest.description: What the test delivery did: whether it connected and wrote the sample file, and the error when it did not.

status.description: The HTTP status your endpoint answered.

id.description: The product id in your store.

workflowId.description: The workflow it is mapped to, if any.

code.description: Machine-readable reason, such as validation_failed, invalid_reference, not_found, in_use, draft_reference.

param.description: The field at fault, as a dotted path (intake.ruleId, accepts.0.preflight.profileId).

details.description: Every problem found, or the records that block a delete.
